assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Indian Oil Corporation (consolidated, Rs crore). Three segments, as reported (gas and 'other business' combined for a consistent history): petroleum products (refining + marketing + pipelines, incl. 51.89%-owned Chennai Petroleum), petrochemicals, gas & other. Segment EBITDA = segment result before FX + segment D&A; 'unallocated' = exchange and derivative losses. Petroleum products revenue = sales volume x realisation per tonne and EBITDA = volume x EBITDA per tonne (the build in `petBuild`, checked against the model in IOC.ctx.js). Net Profit and EPS are attributable to owners on 1,377.16 cr shares (IOC.patch.js); the tax line also carries minorities (CPCL 48.11%), as in UPL/TIINDIA. Investments (Rs73,298 cr at Mar-26 book: listed stakes in ONGC, GAIL, Oil India at fair value; Petronet and ~30 JVs at equity value; Rs6,783 cr of government securities) stay inside treasury (net debt); the SOTP marks the listed stakes to the 30-Sep-2026 close less 20% in a separate line. Valued on a sum of the parts: EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E EBITDA.

segments.name: Petroleum products
segments._why: Revenue net of excise = petroleum sales volume x realisation (see petBuild). Volume +1.5% in FY27E (Q1 petroleum sales 23.48 MMT vs 23.3 a year earlier; LPG demand down ~20% QoQ on supply curbs, ATF down on airspace closures), +3.5% FY28E and +3% FY29E as Panipat, Gujarat and Barauni add ~17 MMTPA of refining (throughput guided 77 / 85 / 90 MMT) and surplus product is exported. Realisation +22.6% in FY27E: the Indian crude basket averaged $100.7/bbl in Q1FY27 vs $83 in Q4FY26 and ~$64 in Q3FY26 (Q1 realisation ~Rs1.02 lakh/t); we assume prices ease through the year. -8% in FY28E as crude normalises, +1% FY29E.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA per tonne of petroleum product sold (consolidated segment EBITDA / standalone petroleum sales incl. exports): Rs5,128 (FY22), 3,849 (FY23), 8,320 (FY24), 3,816 (FY25), 8,634 (FY26); average FY22-26 Rs5,950. FY27E Rs3,800: Q1FY27 segment EBITDA only ~Rs2,000 cr (segment loss Rs1,705 cr after ~Rs3,800 cr of D&A) despite a ~Rs15,000 cr finished-goods inventory gain, because retail prices were held while crude averaged $100; Q2-Q4 need ~Rs4,800/t as LPG under-recovery falls (Rs665/cyl in June, Rs475 in July, ~Rs250 expected for Q2) and the Rs14,486 cr LPG compensation keeps accruing at ~Rs1,207 cr a month to Oct-2026. FY28E Rs5,600 and FY29E Rs5,900: below the FY22-26 average because marketing margins stay political; refining helped by the new capacity (60% / 80% / 100% ramp-up).

segments.name: Petrochemicals
segments._why: Q1FY27 segment revenue Rs9,517 cr (+41% YoY on prices); sales 0.768 MMT vs 0.901 in Q4FY26. The Rs13,805 cr PX-PTA complex at Paradip (94.6% complete at Jun-26, commissioning Aug-26 guided) and the Rs2,949 cr polybutadiene rubber plant at Panipat (Dec-26) add volume from H2FY27. Revenue Rs33,000 / 40,000 / 43,000 cr.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 2.0-3.4% in FY23-FY25 (cyclical trough, Chinese capacity), 8.9% in FY26 (Q4 EBIT Rs1,209 cr, the best ever). Q1FY27 EBIT Rs217 cr (~6% EBITDA margin). We assume 8.5% / 11.25% / 12.1% (EBITDA Rs2,800 / 4,500 / 5,200 cr): PTA is a low-margin commodity, so we stay below FY21-FY22 peaks (32% / 20%).

segments.name: Gas & other businesses
segments._why: Natural gas trading and city gas (gas sales 7.28 MMT in FY26; 1.87 MMT in Q1FY27) plus E&P, explosives, cryogenics and wind/solar. Q1FY27 revenue Rs16,529 cr (gas Rs14,481 cr, other Rs2,048 cr) on LNG prices lifted by Qatar's force majeure. Revenue Rs56,000 / 55,000 / 57,500 cr.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA Rs3,233 cr in FY25 and Rs1,630 cr in FY26 (gas EBITDA only Rs130 cr, a loss before D&A in some quarters); Q1FY27 EBIT Rs1,151 cr (gas Rs526 cr, other Rs625 cr), unusually high. We assume EBITDA Rs3,600 cr in FY27E, then Rs3,000 / 3,200 cr as LNG prices normalise.

petBuild._note: Petroleum products build: volume = standalone petroleum sales incl. exports (MMT); realisation = segment revenue net of excise per tonne; EBITDA per tonne = consolidated segment EBITDA / that volume. Checked against the segment growth and margin above in IOC.ctx.js.
petBuild._throughputWhy: Standalone refinery throughput guided on the Q1FY27 call (1-Aug-2026): ~77 MMT FY27, ~85 MMT FY28, ~90 MMT FY29 (FY26 75.5 MMT). CPCL adds ~10 MMT.

assumptions._unallocWhy: Exchange and derivative losses not in segment EBITDA: Rs8,331 cr in FY26 (rupee fell 11% to 94.84/$), Rs2,439 cr FY25, Rs1,539 cr FY24, Rs7,717 cr FY23. Q1FY27 standalone FX loss only ~Rs100 cr (rupee 94.8 -> ~95.5). We assume Rs1,500 cr a year (~1.5% annual depreciation on ~$12bn of foreign-currency liabilities).
assumptions._capexWhy: Standalone capex budget FY27 Rs32,700 cr (Q1 Rs6,461 cr); management expects Rs30,000-40,000 cr a year for the next 2-3 years (petchem programme ~Rs1 lakh cr over 5-6 years, renewables via Terra Clean, pipelines, CBG, SAF, ships). Consolidated capex was Rs33,157 cr in FY26 (standalone Rs32,405 cr incl. Rs663 cr of equity in JVs). We model Rs34,000 / 32,000 / 32,000 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: D&A Rs18,420 cr in FY26 (6.0% of average gross block of Rs3,05,800 cr; Rs16,777 cr FY25); Q1FY27 Rs4,408 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once and holds CWIP (Rs86,049 cr at Mar-26, mostly the three refinery expansions) flat, which roughly stands in for the ~Rs90,000 cr of projects being capitalised in H2FY27. 5.7% of average gross block gives ~Rs19,000 / 20,900 / 22,700 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: IOC is a net borrower (borrowings incl. leases Rs1,31,822 cr at Mar-26, Rs1,41,453 cr standalone at Jun-26), so interest income is in the other-income line below, not a yield on net cash.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener other income before exceptional items: Rs5,015 cr FY24, Rs5,167 cr FY25, Rs6,695 cr FY26, TTM Jun-26 Rs6,516 cr (Q1FY27 Rs1,143 cr = Rs446 cr other income + Rs697 cr share of JV/associate profit). FY26 build (AR note 39): interest and dividend income Rs3,513 cr (dividends from ONGC, GAIL, Oil India; interest on government securities, loans), share of JV and associate profit Rs2,976 cr (Petronet, Hindustan Urvarak, IndianOil Adani Gas, IOT, others), other Rs640 cr. FY27E Rs6,000 cr (JV share ~Rs2,600 cr, dividends and interest ~Rs3,100 cr after redemption of the oil bonds, other ~Rs300 cr), rising ~5% a year.
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost Rs8,354 cr FY26 (Rs9,311 cr FY25); Q1FY27 Rs1,730 cr. Borrowings rose by ~Rs31,000 cr in Q1FY27 on working capital at higher rates; FY28E rises as interest on the ~Rs90,000 cr of completed projects stops being capitalised.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax line includes minorities (engine workaround). FY26: tax Rs13,795 cr + minorities Rs1,581 cr = 26.8% of PBT (Rs57,472 cr); FY24 27.2%. Statutory rate 25.17%; minorities are 48.11% of CPCL's profit (and 25% of Lanka IOC). FY27E 29% because CPCL (a pure refiner) earns a larger share of a smaller group profit (Q1FY27: minorities Rs490 cr against a group loss).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend payout 31-50% of standalone PAT in FY22-FY26 (31% FY26, 32% FY25); DIPAM's CPSE guideline asks for 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher. We assume 30% of group PAT.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at rf + beta x ERP; IOC carries ~Rs1.3 lakh cr of debt, so we set beta so that the rate equals our WACC: cost of equity 12.5% (beta 1.0), post-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (7.3% x (1-25.2%)), debt 41% of capital at the 30-Sep-2026 market value -> WACC ~9.6%; beta 0.52 gives 9.62%.
dcf._tgWhy: 4%, below the house 5-6% range: Indian fuel demand grows ~3-4% a year now, but EVs, CNG/LNG trucks and ethanol cap petrol and diesel growth over the long run, and IOC's prices are partly set by the government.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades to 5% (nominal, with volume ~2-3% and price ~2%).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 6.0%: Screener-basis margins were 11.0%, 7.9%, 3.6%, 9.7%, 4.8%, 9.8% in FY21-FY26 (average 7.8%); we use a lower mid-cycle because marketing margins are capped by policy in high-crude years and new capacity adds lower-margin petrochemicals.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~3.5% of revenue now and management expects Rs30,000-40,000 cr a year for 2-3 more years (petchem Rs1 lakh cr over 5-6 years, renewables): we hold 3.5% of revenue, above depreciation (2.3%), for the whole period.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The Gulf disruption keeps refining margins high while crude settles near $75: GRMs stay well above pre-war levels, the three expansions ramp on time, the government compensates more of the LPG buffer (Rs29,730 cr negative at Jun-26) and marketing margins recover to the FY24/FY26 level; the market pays its own median multiple again.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Crude stays above $90 with retail prices frozen into state elections, LPG losses are only partly compensated, the expansions slip and stabilise slowly, petchem margins stay weak; earnings stay near trough levels (FY23/FY25) and the stock trades at its lower-quartile multiple.

cover.headline: Cheap on paper, but the cycle and the state set the margins: SELL
cover.lead: Indian Oil refines ~31% of India's crude, owns >20,000 km of pipelines and sells 42% of its fuel. It earned ₹42,096 cr for shareholders in FY26, then lost ₹1,631 cr in Q1FY27 as crude hit US$100/bbl and retail prices were held. The stock looks cheap: 6.8x our FY28E EPS of ₹19.9 and ~0.8x book. But it has always looked cheap: its own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA (after taking out its investments) has a median of 4.2x since Apr-2021, and oil marketers and refiners trade 12.8% below their five-year medians. On 3.5x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹64,215 cr, less net debt and minorities, plus its ONGC, GAIL, Oil India and Petronet stakes at market less 20%, we get **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** The street (median ₹163; ₹150 for the three notes after Q1) uses 4.5-5.5x. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Petroleum-segment EBITDA per tonne sold was ₹3,800 in FY23 and FY25 and ₹8,300-8,600 in FY24 and FY26. The difference was not volume or efficiency but whether retail prices kept up with crude and how wide refining cracks were. In Q1FY27 the government cut excise by ₹10/litre and allowed staggered price rises, yet IOC still lost money before a ~₹15,000 cr inventory gain. We forecast ₹3,800/t in FY27E and ₹5,600-5,900/t after, a little below the FY22-26 average.

arguments.h: The expansions are real; the returns are not guaranteed
arguments.p: ~₹90,000 cr of projects (Panipat 15→25 MMTPA, Gujarat 13.7→18, Barauni 6→9, PX-PTA) are 89-95% complete and due by Dec-2026; throughput is guided at 77 / 85 / 90 MMT for FY27-29. That lifts our petroleum volumes ~3% a year. But capex stays at ₹30,000-40,000 cr a year (petrochemicals next), so free cash flow stays thin: ₹−177 / 10,779 / 17,514 cr in FY27-29E.

arguments.h: Investments are ~₹20 a share, not a free option
arguments.p: The listed stakes are worth ₹34,005 cr at the 30-Sep close (ONGC alone ₹22,284 cr), ₹20 a share after a 20% discount; Petronet and ~30 unlisted JVs (fertiliser, LNG, Russian upstream) add ~₹16 a share at book. Against that, 48% of Chennai Petroleum belongs to others (₹10,287 cr at market) and net debt was ~₹54,000 cr even after counting every investment.

arguments.h: Valuation: we follow the street's method, not its multiple
arguments.p: The street adds investments to 4.5-5.5x EBITDA. IOC's own history says the market pays ~4.2x for the operating business once the stakes are taken out (5.2x if they are left in), and the sector trades below its averages. 3.5x gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the stock at ₹135 prices ~3.9x FY28E core EBITDA, i.e. our FY28E earnings with little discount for another policy squeeze. Cross-checks: P/E ₹105, DCF ₹197 (only if mid-cycle margins hold for a decade).

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): marketing margins after the May-June price rises, LPG under-recovery (~₹250/cylinder guided), inventory effects, debt after the Q1 jump.
Commissioning of Gujarat (Nov-2026), Panipat and Barauni (Dec-2026) and PX-PTA: first crude in, then a 60% / 80% / 100% ramp over three years.
Government decisions: retail price changes, SAED and export duties (reviewed fortnightly), compensation for the ₹29,730 cr negative LPG buffer.
Crude and the Strait of Hormuz: each US$10/bbl moves IOC's working capital and its marketing margin.
Board appointments: independent directors and a reconstituted Audit Committee.

sections.title: India's largest refiner, pipeline owner and fuel retailer, majority-owned by the state

blocks.p: Indian Oil Corporation (IndianOil) is a Maharatna public-sector company: the Government owns 51.5% and two other state companies (ONGC and Oil India) a further 19.4%. It runs 10 refineries including Chennai Petroleum (51.89%), with 80.75 MMTPA of capacity (~31% of India's 258.1 MMTPA), moves crude and products through >20,000 km of pipelines (5,300 km crude, 13,300 km products, 1,300 km gas) and sells through 43,138 fuel stations, LPG distributors and aviation stations. In FY26 it sold 105.117 MMT of products, 42% of India's petroleum sales (54% of jet fuel, 46% of LPG).

blocks.p: Two things make IOC different from a private refiner. First, it is integrated end to end: it refines ~75 MMT itself, buys the rest of what it sells from CPCL, other refiners and imports, and carries most of it by its own pipelines. Second, its retail prices for petrol, diesel and household LPG are, in practice, decided with the Government. When crude spikes the state can ask the three PSU marketers (IOC, BPCL, HPCL) to hold prices and absorb the loss, and compensates them later, partly or not at all. Petroleum products are therefore one business with two very different margin pools: a refining margin set by global cracks and a marketing margin set in Delhi. IOC does not report them separately.

sections.title: A growing fuel market with administered prices, hit by the 2026 Gulf war

blocks.p: India refining capacity 258.1 MMTPA (FY26), throughput 272.1 MMT; IOC group 80.75 MMTPA (~31%), going to ~98 MMTPA by FY28. Petroleum product consumption +2% in FY26 (diesel +4%, petrol +6%); in Q1FY27 petrol +7% and diesel +5% QoQ, ATF -5%, LPG -20% (commercial supply curbs). India imports most of its crude (and much of its LPG and LNG), so the rupee and the Gulf matter as much as demand.

US-Iran conflict from end-Feb 2026: Strait of Hormuz traffic disrupted, Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG under force majeure. Indian basket US$63.87 (Q3FY26) -> US$83.01 (Q4FY26) -> US$100.74/bbl (Q1FY27). Government cut SAED on petrol and diesel by ₹10/litre on 27-Mar-2026 and re-imposed export duties on diesel and ATF; retail prices raised in tranches from May-2026 (~₹3/litre each at first, ~₹7.5 on diesel cumulatively per the Q1 call). A 60-day US-Iran truce from mid-June eased prices before renewed escalation.

Petrol and diesel prices are formally deregulated but in practice set by the three PSU OMCs with the government's consent; prices were held for long stretches, including through the 2026 Gulf war. Household LPG is sold below cost and losses are compensated by the government case by case: in Oct-2025 MoPNG approved ₹14,486 cr for IOC for under-recoveries up to Mar-2026, paid in 12 monthly instalments from Nov-2025.

sections.title: Petroleum products: 95% of EBITDA, two margin pools, one of them political

blocks.p: The petroleum segment refines crude (IOC standalone 75.451 MMT in FY26 at 107% utilisation, plus CPCL ~10 MMT), carries it through IOC's pipelines (105.556 MMT in FY26) and sells it (88.967 MMT in India, 5.213 MMT exported). Its EBITDA is the sum of a refining margin (GRM: product value less crude cost, US$/bbl), a marketing margin (retail price less the refinery-gate price, taxes and dealer commission, ₹/litre), pipeline tariffs and inventory gains or losses, less operating costs. IOC disclosed GRM until Q3FY26 (US$12.05/bbl in FY24, US$4.80 in FY25) and has paused it "while volatility lasts"; it has never disclosed the marketing margin.

blocks.h: Refining: bigger, more complex, and taxed when it booms

blocks.p: Three expansions add ~17 MMTPA (+21%) to IOC's refining: Panipat 15→25 MMTPA (₹38,231 cr, 94% complete), Gujarat 13.7→18 (₹18,936 cr, 89%) and Barauni 6→9 (₹18,113 cr, 92%), all due Nov-Dec 2026, with a 60% / 80% / 100% ramp-up over three years. Management guides throughput of 77 / 85 / 90 MMT for FY27-29 and expects higher distillate yields (79-80% now) and lower fuel & loss (8.0% in Q1FY27, the lowest since BS-VI). The 2026 war pushed product cracks very high: Q1FY27 GRM was US$36/bbl before the special export duty and US$15.59 after it (crude inventory loss US$3-4/bbl). The state took most of the windfall through the export duty, as it did with the 2022 windfall tax.

blocks.h: Marketing: volumes grow, margins are decided elsewhere

blocks.p: IOC sells ~42% of India's petroleum products through 43,138 fuel stations (Jun-2026) and ~46% of its LPG. Volumes grew 4.7% in FY26, ahead of the market. But in Q1FY27 retail prices were held while the crude basket averaged US$100.74/bbl: LPG under-recovery reached ₹670/cylinder in May and ₹665 in June, then ~₹475 in July; petrol and diesel lost money until price rises in tranches from May (the SAED cut of ₹10/litre on 27-Mar helped). The quarter's EBITDA (₹4,062 cr consolidated) was only positive because of a ~₹15,000 cr gain on finished-goods inventory. IOC expects LPG losses to fall to ~₹250/cylinder in Q2 and is "confident" of compensation, but the timing and amount are the Government's call: the negative LPG buffer stood at ₹29,730 cr at Jun-2026.

blocks.callout: **Our forecast:** petroleum EBITDA of ₹36,325 / 55,406 / 60,125 cr (₹3800 / 5600 / 5900 per tonne). FY27E assumes Q2-Q4 average ~₹4,800/t after Q1's ~₹850/t: falling LPG losses, retail prices that roughly cover cost, refining margins well above pre-war levels but taxed. FY28-29E sit ~6% below the FY22-26 average of ₹5,949/t. Each ₹500/t is ~₹4,947 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~₹3 of EPS).

sections.title: Petrochemicals and gas: 5% of EBITDA today, where the next ₹1 lakh cr goes

blocks.p: Petrochemicals (polymers, PX, PTA, LAB, glycols) earned segment EBITDA of ₹6,137 cr in FY21 and ₹5,550 cr in FY22, then ₹716-949 cr a year in FY23-FY25 (2-3% margins) as Chinese capacity flooded the market, and ₹2,495 cr in FY26 (Q4 EBIT ₹1,209 cr, the best ever). Q1FY27 EBIT was ₹217 cr on 0.77 MMT. The ₹13,805 cr PX-PTA complex at Paradip (95% complete) and the ₹2,949 cr polybutadiene rubber plant at Panipat start in FY27; another ~₹1 lakh cr of petchem projects (petchem intensity 6.5% → 15%) is planned to FY30. We forecast EBITDA of ₹2,800 / 4,500 / 5,200 cr.

Gas (LNG and natural gas trading, city gas) and other businesses (E&P, explosives, cryogenics, wind and solar) earned ₹3,233 cr in FY25 and ₹1,630 cr in FY26 (gas alone only ₹130 cr). Q1FY27 was unusually strong (EBIT: gas ₹526 cr, other ₹625 cr). We forecast ₹3,600 / 3,000 / 3,200 cr. The bigger long-term bets sit in joint ventures and are in our valuation at book: IndianOil LNG (Ennore terminal), IndianOil-Adani Gas, Hindustan Urvarak (fertiliser), Terra Clean (renewables, 2.65 GW of grid connectivity) and the Russian and Abu Dhabi upstream stakes.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** IOC has the strongest physical franchise in Indian oil, and nobody will take its volumes. But a moat that does not let you set prices does not earn excess returns through the cycle: ROE averaged ~18% in FY22-FY26 (standalone 22.6%, 7.1%, 29.8%, 8.7%, 22.7%), close to the cost of equity once the trough years are weighted honestly.

sections.title: Boom, bust, boom, bust, boom: EBITDA of ₹31,000-77,000 cr in alternate years

blocks.p: IOC's revenue follows the crude price (₹3.6 lakh cr in FY21, ₹8.4 lakh cr in FY23, ₹7.8 lakh cr in FY26, net of excise), so revenue growth says little. What matters is the margin per tonne, and it swings with two things IOC does not control: refining margins (cracks) and how far the government lets retail prices follow crude. EBITDA was ₹46,619 cr in FY22, ₹30,683 cr in FY23 (retail prices held while crude spiked after the Ukraine war), ₹75,650 cr in FY24 (crude fell, prices did not), ₹36,040 cr in FY25 (refining margins collapsed to US$4.80/bbl) and ₹77,108 cr in FY26. Profit attributable to shareholders went ₹25,102 → 9,792 → 41,730 → 13,598 → 42,096 cr. Two of the last five years were troughs; Q1FY27 (a loss) starts a third.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** IOC has no "normal" year to forecast from; the right base is a cycle average. Over FY22-FY26 petroleum-segment EBITDA averaged ~₹5,950 per tonne sold (₹3,800 in trough years, ₹8,300-8,600 in good years). We forecast ₹3,800/t for FY27E (Q1 was close to zero before inventory gains), then ₹5,600/t and ₹5,900/t as the expansions add volume, i.e. slightly below the five-year average because the 2026 war showed again that marketing margins are a policy decision.

blocks.p: In the Jun-2026 quarter the Indian crude basket averaged US$100.74/bbl (US$83.01 in Q4FY26) and retail prices rose only in tranches. blocks.p: Over FY24-FY26 IOC generated ₹1,81,740 cr of operating cash and spent ₹1,00,505 cr on capex and ₹34,220 cr on dividends; over FY21-FY23 ₹1,03,864 cr, ₹78,425 cr and ₹22,585 cr. Management does not plan a pause: it guides ₹30,000-40,000 cr a year for another 2-3 years (petrochemicals ~₹1 lakh cr over 5-6 years, renewables, CBG, SAF, ships). Returns follow the cycle: ROE 22.7% in FY26 and 8.7% in FY25 (standalone), 29.8% in FY24 and 7.1% in FY23.

sections.title: Earnings quality: inventory gains, compensation timing and FX move profit by thousands of crores

blocks.p: The accounts are audited by C&AG-appointed firms and are unqualified, but four items make reported profit a poor guide to the run-rate: (1) **inventory gains and losses**: IOC carries ~₹1.2 lakh cr of inventory, so a US$10/bbl move in crude swings profit by thousands of crores (Q1FY27: ~₹15,000 cr finished-goods gain, crude loss of US$3-4/bbl); (2) **LPG compensation**: the ₹14,486 cr approved in Oct-2025 is booked in monthly instalments (₹6,036 cr in FY26, ₹3,622 cr in Q1FY27) while the cumulative negative buffer of ₹29,730 cr is not on the balance sheet; (3) **exchange losses** of ₹8,331 cr in FY26 sit outside segment results; (4) Screener adds **exceptional items** (₹1,945 cr in FY25) to other income. Screener also shows profit before minorities; we use profit to owners and IOC's own share count (1,377.16 cr, excluding the 34.97 cr treasury shares in the IOC Shares Trust).

blocks.p: House rule (PLAYBOOK §4, §7c): start from the stock's own one-year-forward multiple from Apr-2021 to 30-Sep-2026, leave out trough years, then apply the sector's move against its five-year medians. Because the street values IOC on EV/EBITDA plus investments, we measure the same thing: EV less ALL investments at their latest book value (so the stakes we add back separately are not counted twice), divided by the next full year's consolidated EBITDA (realised for past years, our FY27E-FY28E for recent dates), on every weekly close. FY25 is left out as a trough (EBITDA ₹36,040 cr, below half of FY24's ₹75,650 cr). Our 3.5x applies to EBITDA before other income, like the street's.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Indian Oil Corporation (consolidated, Rs crore). Three segments, as reported (gas and 'other business' combined for a consistent history): petroleum products (refining + marketing + pipelines, incl. 51.89%-owned Chennai Petroleum), petrochemicals, gas & other. Segment EBITDA = segment result before FX + segment D&A; 'unallocated' = exchange and derivative losses. Petroleum products revenue = sales volume x realisation per tonne and EBITDA = volume x EBITDA per tonne (the build in `petBuild`, checked against the model in IOC.ctx.js). Net Profit and EPS are attributable to owners on 1,377.16 cr shares (IOC.patch.js); the tax line also carries minorities (CPCL 48.11%), as in UPL/TIINDIA. Investments (Rs73,298 cr at Mar-26 book: listed stakes in ONGC, GAIL, Oil India at fair value; Petronet and ~30 JVs at equity value; Rs6,783 cr of government securities) stay inside treasury (net debt); the SOTP marks the listed stakes to the 30-Sep-2026 close less 20% in a separate line. Valued on a sum of the parts: EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E EBITDA.

segments.name: Petroleum products
segments._why: Revenue net of excise = petroleum sales volume x realisation (see petBuild). Volume +1.5% in FY27E (Q1 petroleum sales 23.48 MMT vs 23.3 a year earlier; LPG demand down ~20% QoQ on supply curbs, ATF down on airspace closures), +3.5% FY28E and +3% FY29E as Panipat, Gujarat and Barauni add ~17 MMTPA of refining (throughput guided 77 / 85 / 90 MMT) and surplus product is exported. Realisation +22.6% in FY27E: the Indian crude basket averaged $100.7/bbl in Q1FY27 vs $83 in Q4FY26 and ~$64 in Q3FY26 (Q1 realisation ~Rs1.02 lakh/t); we assume prices ease through the year. -8% in FY28E as crude normalises, +1% FY29E.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA per tonne of petroleum product sold (consolidated segment EBITDA / standalone petroleum sales incl. exports): Rs5,128 (FY22), 3,849 (FY23), 8,320 (FY24), 3,816 (FY25), 8,634 (FY26); average FY22-26 Rs5,950. FY27E Rs3,800: Q1FY27 segment EBITDA only ~Rs2,000 cr (segment loss Rs1,705 cr after ~Rs3,800 cr of D&A) despite a ~Rs15,000 cr finished-goods inventory gain, because retail prices were held while crude averaged $100; Q2-Q4 need ~Rs4,800/t as LPG under-recovery falls (Rs665/cyl in June, Rs475 in July, ~Rs250 expected for Q2) and the Rs14,486 cr LPG compensation keeps accruing at ~Rs1,207 cr a month to Oct-2026. FY28E Rs5,600 and FY29E Rs5,900: below the FY22-26 average because marketing margins stay political; refining helped by the new capacity (60% / 80% / 100% ramp-up).

segments.name: Petrochemicals
segments._why: Q1FY27 segment revenue Rs9,517 cr (+41% YoY on prices); sales 0.768 MMT vs 0.901 in Q4FY26. The Rs13,805 cr PX-PTA complex at Paradip (94.6% complete at Jun-26, commissioning Aug-26 guided) and the Rs2,949 cr polybutadiene rubber plant at Panipat (Dec-26) add volume from H2FY27. Revenue Rs33,000 / 40,000 / 43,000 cr.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 2.0-3.4% in FY23-FY25 (cyclical trough, Chinese capacity), 8.9% in FY26 (Q4 EBIT Rs1,209 cr, the best ever). Q1FY27 EBIT Rs217 cr (~6% EBITDA margin). We assume 8.5% / 11.25% / 12.1% (EBITDA Rs2,800 / 4,500 / 5,200 cr): PTA is a low-margin commodity, so we stay below FY21-FY22 peaks (32% / 20%).

segments.name: Gas & other businesses
segments._why: Natural gas trading and city gas (gas sales 7.28 MMT in FY26; 1.87 MMT in Q1FY27) plus E&P, explosives, cryogenics and wind/solar. Q1FY27 revenue Rs16,529 cr (gas Rs14,481 cr, other Rs2,048 cr) on LNG prices lifted by Qatar's force majeure. Revenue Rs56,000 / 55,000 / 57,500 cr.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA Rs3,233 cr in FY25 and Rs1,630 cr in FY26 (gas EBITDA only Rs130 cr, a loss before D&A in some quarters); Q1FY27 EBIT Rs1,151 cr (gas Rs526 cr, other Rs625 cr), unusually high. We assume EBITDA Rs3,600 cr in FY27E, then Rs3,000 / 3,200 cr as LNG prices normalise.

petBuild._note: Petroleum products build: volume = standalone petroleum sales incl. exports (MMT); realisation = segment revenue net of excise per tonne; EBITDA per tonne = consolidated segment EBITDA / that volume. Checked against the segment growth and margin above in IOC.ctx.js.
petBuild._throughputWhy: Standalone refinery throughput guided on the Q1FY27 call (1-Aug-2026): ~77 MMT FY27, ~85 MMT FY28, ~90 MMT FY29 (FY26 75.5 MMT). CPCL adds ~10 MMT.

assumptions._unallocWhy: Exchange and derivative losses not in segment EBITDA: Rs8,331 cr in FY26 (rupee fell 11% to 94.84/$), Rs2,439 cr FY25, Rs1,539 cr FY24, Rs7,717 cr FY23. Q1FY27 standalone FX loss only ~Rs100 cr (rupee 94.8 -> ~95.5). We assume Rs1,500 cr a year (~1.5% annual depreciation on ~$12bn of foreign-currency liabilities).
assumptions._capexWhy: Standalone capex budget FY27 Rs32,700 cr (Q1 Rs6,461 cr); management expects Rs30,000-40,000 cr a year for the next 2-3 years (petchem programme ~Rs1 lakh cr over 5-6 years, renewables via Terra Clean, pipelines, CBG, SAF, ships). Consolidated capex was Rs33,157 cr in FY26 (standalone Rs32,405 cr incl. Rs663 cr of equity in JVs). We model Rs34,000 / 32,000 / 32,000 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: D&A Rs18,420 cr in FY26 (6.0% of average gross block of Rs3,05,800 cr; Rs16,777 cr FY25); Q1FY27 Rs4,408 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once and holds CWIP (Rs86,049 cr at Mar-26, mostly the three refinery expansions) flat, which roughly stands in for the ~Rs90,000 cr of projects being capitalised in H2FY27. 5.7% of average gross block gives ~Rs19,000 / 20,900 / 22,700 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: IOC is a net borrower (borrowings incl. leases Rs1,31,822 cr at Mar-26, Rs1,41,453 cr standalone at Jun-26), so interest income is in the other-income line below, not a yield on net cash.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener other income before exceptional items: Rs5,015 cr FY24, Rs5,167 cr FY25, Rs6,695 cr FY26, TTM Jun-26 Rs6,516 cr (Q1FY27 Rs1,143 cr = Rs446 cr other income + Rs697 cr share of JV/associate profit). FY26 build (AR note 39): interest and dividend income Rs3,513 cr (dividends from ONGC, GAIL, Oil India; interest on government securities, loans), share of JV and associate profit Rs2,976 cr (Petronet, Hindustan Urvarak, IndianOil Adani Gas, IOT, others), other Rs640 cr. FY27E Rs6,000 cr (JV share ~Rs2,600 cr, dividends and interest ~Rs3,100 cr after redemption of the oil bonds, other ~Rs300 cr), rising ~5% a year.
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost Rs8,354 cr FY26 (Rs9,311 cr FY25); Q1FY27 Rs1,730 cr. Borrowings rose by ~Rs31,000 cr in Q1FY27 on working capital at higher rates; FY28E rises as interest on the ~Rs90,000 cr of completed projects stops being capitalised.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax line includes minorities (engine workaround). FY26: tax Rs13,795 cr + minorities Rs1,581 cr = 26.8% of PBT (Rs57,472 cr); FY24 27.2%. Statutory rate 25.17%; minorities are 48.11% of CPCL's profit (and 25% of Lanka IOC). FY27E 29% because CPCL (a pure refiner) earns a larger share of a smaller group profit (Q1FY27: minorities Rs490 cr against a group loss).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend payout 31-50% of standalone PAT in FY22-FY26 (31% FY26, 32% FY25); DIPAM's CPSE guideline asks for 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher. We assume 30% of group PAT.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at rf + beta x ERP; IOC carries ~Rs1.3 lakh cr of debt, so we set beta so that the rate equals our WACC: cost of equity 12.5% (beta 1.0), post-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (7.3% x (1-25.2%)), debt 41% of capital at the 30-Sep-2026 market value -> WACC ~9.6%; beta 0.52 gives 9.62%.
dcf._tgWhy: 4%, below the house 5-6% range: Indian fuel demand grows ~3-4% a year now, but EVs, CNG/LNG trucks and ethanol cap petrol and diesel growth over the long run, and IOC's prices are partly set by the government.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades to 5% (nominal, with volume ~2-3% and price ~2%).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 6.0%: Screener-basis margins were 11.0%, 7.9%, 3.6%, 9.7%, 4.8%, 9.8% in FY21-FY26 (average 7.8%); we use a lower mid-cycle because marketing margins are capped by policy in high-crude years and new capacity adds lower-margin petrochemicals.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~3.5% of revenue now and management expects Rs30,000-40,000 cr a year for 2-3 more years (petchem Rs1 lakh cr over 5-6 years, renewables): we hold 3.5% of revenue, above depreciation (2.3%), for the whole period.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The Gulf disruption keeps refining margins high while crude settles near $75: GRMs stay well above pre-war levels, the three expansions ramp on time, the government compensates more of the LPG buffer (Rs29,730 cr negative at Jun-26) and marketing margins recover to the FY24/FY26 level; the market pays its own median multiple again.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Crude stays above $90 with retail prices frozen into state elections, LPG losses are only partly compensated, the expansions slip and stabilise slowly, petchem margins stay weak; earnings stay near trough levels (FY23/FY25) and the stock trades at its lower-quartile multiple.
